question: Who had Sialkot as his capital?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Menander__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Menander I, also known as Milinda, was an Indo-Greek King who ruled in the Northwestern regions of South Asia during the 2nd century BCE.
 
• His reign is noted for the expansion of the Indo-Greek territories and for his patronage of Buddhist culture, which is famously recorded in the Buddhist text "Milinda Panha" or "The Questions of Milinda".
 
• Sialkot, located in present-day Pakistan, served as a significant center and possibly as his capital during his reign, highlighting the extent of Greek influence in the region.
 
• Menander's rule is often considered a golden age of Hellenistic influence in the East, combining Greek and Buddhist cultures, and fostering trade along the Silk Road.
